key_insight: A drilled-to-bossed joint geometry combined with optimized DDFW settings substantially improves AA2024-T351 weld strength, and a deep learning ensemble can predict tensile performance with useful accuracy.
engineering_relevance: The study shows that joint geometry plus process tuning can raise weld integrity in lightweight aerospace-grade aluminum while reducing reliance on trial-and-error parameter selection.
method: Used an L18 orthogonal array to study friction pressure, forging pressure, spindle speed, faying-surface geometry, and friction time.
Compared drilled-to-bossed versus conventional flat-to-flat joint designs in direct drive friction welding.
Trained deep learning models, including an ensemble residual network, attention network, and adaptive multiscale network, to predict ultimate tensile strength.
evidence_signal: The best reported condition achieved 538 MPa tensile strength and 325 MPa torsional strength, while the ensemble residual network reached an R² of about 0.81.
watch_item: The reported predictive accuracy is moderate and likely depends on the limited experimental design, so broader validation is needed before deployment on new materials or weld setups.
paper_title: Enhancing weld performance of AA2024-T351 using drilled-to-bossed geometry and deep learning prediction in direct drive friction welding
